title: Two arrows per node
summary: A doubly linked list keeps next and prev, so it can be walked both ways.

checkpoints.text: 20 is the only node. Both of its arrows are NULL: nothing comes after it, and nothing comes before it.
Adding 10 at the front. The old first node (20) now points back at the new node: its `prev` arrow is drawn in amber, `next` arrows in teal.
`head` moves to 10. Adding at the front changed four pointers: the new node's two, the old head's `prev`, and `head` itself.
30 is hung after 20 and points back at it. Every link now exists in both directions.
After the forward walk, `last` is at 30. Walking backwards follows `prev` arrows, which a singly linked list does not have.
10 20 30 | 30 20 10: the same nodes forwards and backwards. The price is one extra pointer in every node.
